prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, using designed small molecules to direct the ubiquitin-proteasome system to chosen proteins

statement.case_for: Targeted protein degradation is a new chemical modality: a small molecule is designed to bring a chosen protein and an E3 ligase into proximity so that the cell's own proteasome machinery removes the target. The mechanistic logic is clean, the chemistry is rich (ternary-complex cooperativity, ligase ligand design, the cereblon mechanism of thalidomide-type glues), and the concept has been independently reproduced by many groups over two decades. Four of eight members placed it first and a fifth placed it third, and the support rests on the same scientific argument rather than on mere familiarity. The Crews-Deshaies-Handa configuration pairs the heterobifunctional PROTAC concept with the molecular-glue half of the field, which is what the Aili, Chabes and Brzezinski openings also proposed.
statement.case_against: No degrader is approved yet, so clinical impact is still forward-looking and the prize could be judged early. Attribution is the harder problem: a three-person limit omits Ciulli (VHL ligands, ternary-complex structure), Sakamoto (the first PROTAC paper with Crews and Deshaies), Gray, and Ito and Kim on the cereblon side. Whichever three are chosen, one of the strands will look under-credited. I also hold my own memory of priority claims with some caution.

responses.point: Aqvist backs B023 first but names Ciulli as the third laureate for the VHL ligand and ternary-complex structural work that made PROTACs a drug-like platform, and he rates the timing as slightly early.
responses.response: I opened with Ciulli myself and take the structural-chemistry argument seriously. On reflection I weigh the cereblon mechanism more heavily than I did. Handa's identification of cereblon as the thalidomide target is a discrete mechanistic discovery that explains a whole class of molecular glues and degraders, whereas Ciulli's work refines and generalises a platform whose concept is already carried by Crews and Deshaies. I do not think this is clear-cut, and if the committee prefers Ciulli I would not object. I agree with Aqvist that timing is slightly early, but the mechanism is settled and I do not think waiting improves the science.

responses.point: Somfai places B002 (Pd-catalysed C-N coupling by Buchwald and Hartwig) first as fully mature, general, ubiquitous at process scale, and arguably overdue, and ranks B023 only eighth.
responses.response: I agree B002 is the strongest case on maturity and breadth, and it is my first alternative. Maturity is not the only criterion, though. The 2010 prize already honoured Pd cross-coupling, so this would be an extension of a recognised field with an essentially two-person attribution, Kosugi aside. Targeted degradation opens a new modality and a new mechanism of action. Our eight votes cannot settle whether we should reward a late, safe achievement or a fresher conceptual one. I put more weight on conceptual novelty, and I would accept B002 if the committee judges that clinical immaturity counts against B023.

responses.point: Brzezinski ranks proton-coupled electron transfer (B028) first as a unifying physical-chemical concept with decades of experimental and theoretical confirmation, and places B023 third because clinical validation is still emerging.
responses.response: PCET is intellectually attractive and mature, and I accept that it is the strongest candidate on pure physical-chemical grounds. I still do not favour it, because it is a framework spread across enzymology, theory and electrocatalysis. A short citation that credits a single identifiable advance to three people is harder to write. Even so, I read Brzezinski's clinical-validation caveat as the best argument against my preferred configuration, and I cannot fully answer it. It is why I keep a mature alternative in view.

responses.point: Sparr ranks ionizable lipid nanoparticles (B041) first as a lipid self-assembly achievement in physical chemistry, and notes that the 2023 Medicine prize did not recognise the delivery vehicle.
responses.response: The lipid-nanoparticle case is convincing as physical chemistry, and the clinical validation at global scale is stronger than anything B023 can currently show. My reservation is attribution: the Vancouver core of Cullis, Hope and Madden is credible, but the line to Anderson, Langer and MacLachlan is hard to draw, and the 2023 Medicine prize leaves the committee with a question about overlap. I do not rank B041 above B023, but I would like Sparr to say whether she regards the Vancouver trio as a complete attribution.

uncertainties: Whether the committee should treat the cereblon and thalidomide molecular-glue strand as co-equal with PROTACs, and so whether Handa or Ciulli should hold the third place.
Whether the absence of an approved PROTAC drug makes recognition premature compared with mature candidates such as B002.
Whether the 2010 Pd cross-coupling prize reduces appetite for B002 enough to outweigh its maturity.
My recollection of detailed priority claims is not independently verified.
statement.conflict_note: As chair I preside over the discussion, but I do not see a specific personal or institutional connection to the shortlisted candidates in my profile (Lund; nanophysics and thermoelectrics). Two colleagues, Somfai and Sparr, are also at Lund, which is not a conflict with any candidate. No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile.
